diff_summary.new_string:
Retire when nothing else is writing to the ledger. Reading, archiving, and
removing a chain are not one atomic step, so a governed edit that lands mid
retirement would otherwise have its receipt deleted without ever reaching the
archive. Retirement moves the chain aside rather than deleting it and re-checks
it against the archive before committing, so that case is refused and the chain
is restored exactly as it was, but the retry is yours to run.

The archive is a directory holding whichever segments existed.

oracle.reasoning: The proposed change edits README.md, adding a prose paragraph that documents the ledger retirement race-condition handling: retirement moves the chain aside rather than deleting it, re-checks against the archive before committing, and refuses/restores if a governed edit lands mid-retirement. The Challenger returned CLEAR with no findings and the Defender confirmed CLEAR. I independently evaluated the change against all eight constraints. This is a documentation-only change containing no executable code, so the code-oriented constraints (C-001 error handling, C-003 dependencies, C-004 type safety, C-005 test coverage, C-006 secrets) have no surface to which they apply. C-007 (Governance Pipeline Integrity) and C-008 (Ledger Immutability) are the most relevant: the added text describes retirement behavior that is fully consistent with C-008's bounded exception (retirement is not deletion, the chain is preserved and restored if a conflict is detected, verification occurs before committing) and with the CLAUDE.md description of ledger/retire.py. The documentation strengthens rather than weakens the described enforcement by making the mid-retirement refusal and restoration explicit. C-002 (Scope Boundary) is satisfied: the change is a single coherent documentation edit to one file within the project's stated scope, with no unrelated edits bundled in.
